AI assistant in your terminal

Usage: kiro-cli chat [OPTIONS] [INPUT]

Arguments:
  [INPUT]
          The first question to ask

Options:
  -r, --resume
          Resume the most recent conversation from this directory

      --resume-id <SESSION_ID>
          Resume a specific conversation by session ID

      --resume-picker
          Interactively select a conversation to resume from this directory

      --sessions
          Launch straight into the session dashboard (V3/KAS only); closing it exits rather than
          dropping into a chat

      --agent <AGENT>
          Context profile to use

      --model <MODEL>
          Current model to use

      --effort <EFFORT>
          Initial effort level (e.g. low, medium, high, xhigh, max)

  -a, --trust-all-tools
          Allows the model to use any tool to run commands without asking for confirmation

      --trust-tools <TOOL_NAMES>
          Trust only this set of tools. Example: trust some tools: '--trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write',
          trust no tools: '--trust-tools='. An entry is a tool name, '@server' or '@server/tool' for
          MCP tools, '@builtin', or a '*'/'?' pattern, and trusts a tool on any path it would ask
          about, outside the workspace too. With --no-interactive the v3 engine also takes V2 names,
          and V2 the v3 shell ids and patterns naming them; on v3 a V2 name such as fs_write trusts
          every tool in its permission capability, deleting files included, but fs_read never trusts
          the code tool, and grep, glob, code and introspect trust only their own tools

      --no-interactive
          Whether the command should run without expecting user input

      --trust-workspace
          Skip the "Trust this workspace?" prompt for this launch only (V3 only). Hooks, agents, MCP
          servers and workflows from this folder load without asking; the decision is not saved, so
          a folder that is not already trusted asks again next launch

  -l, --list-sessions
          List all saved chat sessions for the current directory

      --all-cwds
          With --list-sessions: span every workspace (local stores only), emitting one envelope per
          cwd in JSON output

      --list-models
          List available models and exit

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format for list commands (used with --list-models and --list-sessions)

          Possible values:
          - plain:       Outputs the results as markdown
          - json:        Outputs the results as JSON
          - json-pretty: Outputs the results as pretty print JSON
          
          [default: plain]

      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
          Response stream format: text (default), or stream-json for JSON Lines on stdout. 
          stream-json implies --no-interactive

          Possible values:
          - text:        Human-readable text
          - stream-json: The run's ACP events as JSON Lines on stdout, one self-describing event per
            line
          
          [default: text]

  -d, --delete-session <SESSION_ID>
          Delete a saved chat session by ID

      --session-source <v1|v2>
          Target only v1 or v2 store for --delete-session (default: both)
          
          [possible values: v1, v2]

  -w, --wrap <WRAP>
          Control line wrapping behavior (default: auto-detect)

          Possible values:
          - always: Always wrap at terminal width
          - never:  Never wrap (raw output)
          - auto:   Auto-detect based on output target (default)

      --require-mcp-startup
          Require all enabled MCP servers to start successfully; exit with code 3 if any fail

      --tui
          Use the new terminal UI

      --legacy-ui
          Use the legacy harness
          
          [aliases: --classic]

      --agent-engine <ENGINE>
          Agent engine to use: "v1", "v2", or "v3".
          
          Classic (v1) no longer runs: "v1" and a Classic UI choice (--legacy-ui, or KIRO_CHAT_UI or
          chat.ui set to anything but tui) ask to upgrade interactively and take the headless
          default otherwise. A v2 or v3 chat.agentEngine setting takes their place, except that "v1"
          ignores one from a KIRO_DEFAULT_SETTINGS file. When nothing selects an engine: v3
          interactively, where a 2.0 user is asked to choose first and stays on v2 while that prompt
          cannot be shown; v2 with --no-interactive or piped stdin (v3 with --trust-all-tools); v2
          for a --resume-id of a v1 or v2 session and on systems that cannot run v3
          
          [possible values: v2, v1, v3]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity

      --v3
          Launch the next generation Kiro agent

      --v2
          Use the V2 agent engine

      --mode <MODE>
          Mode to use with the V3 agent: "default" or "spec"
          
          [possible values: default, spec]

      --cloud
          Run this session in a cloud sandbox (V3/KAS only), interactively or with --no-interactive.
          Sends _meta.kiro.executionTarget on session/new

      --repo <REPO>
          Repository to open in a cloud session, as name or owner/name (comma-separated for
          multiple). Only meaningful with --cloud

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
